weeks.blurb: Set up your toolchain and ship your first public commit.
Think in components. Make interfaces that respond.
Real users, real sessions, real databases.
Live data, animation, and interfaces that feel alive.
Make it fast. Prove it doesn't break.
One product, end to end, in public.
Your portfolio piece and recruiter handoff.

days.title: Your first public commit
days.focus: Set up Git, create a public repo, and push a README that states what you'll build for 60 days.

days.title: Semantic HTML resume
days.focus: Build a one-page resume using only semantic HTML. No divs allowed.

days.title: Flexbox layout drills
days.focus: Recreate three real app layouts using Flexbox only.

days.title: Responsive grid gallery
days.focus: A photo grid that works at 390px, 768px and 1440px without a single media query hack.

days.title: JavaScript in the DOM
days.focus: Build a todo list with vanilla JS. Add, complete, delete, persist to localStorage.

days.title: Array methods workout
days.focus: Solve 10 data-shaping problems using map, filter, reduce. No for-loops.

days.title: Week 1 ship: personal site
days.focus: Deploy your personal site to a live URL. This is the first thing a recruiter will open.

days.title: Your first React component
days.focus: Set up a React app and build a reusable Card component with props.

days.title: State and events
days.focus: Build a counter, a toggle and a controlled input. Understand re-renders.

days.title: Lists, keys and conditional UI
days.focus: Render a list from JSON with empty, loading and error states.

days.title: Forms that don't fight users
days.focus: A signup form with inline validation, clear errors and a disabled-until-valid submit.

days.title: Build a streak calendar
days.focus: Render 60 days of activity as a heat-map calendar that reads your JSON and stays legible at 390px.

days.title: Lift state up
days.focus: Two sibling components sharing one source of truth. Filter a list from a search box.

days.title: Week 2 ship: component library
days.focus: Package your Button, Card, Input and Badge into a documented mini design system.

days.title: Fetch and render
days.focus: Call a public API, render results, handle the loading state properly.

days.title: Error and empty states
days.focus: Break your own API calls on purpose and design what the user sees.

days.title: Search with debounce
days.focus: A search box that doesn't hammer the API on every keystroke.

days.title: Pagination and infinite scroll
days.focus: Load 500 records without freezing the browser.

days.title: Build your own API
days.focus: Three REST endpoints with a Node server. GET, POST, DELETE.

days.title: Connect a database
days.focus: Persist your API data. Postgres, SQLite or Mongo, your pick.

days.title: Week 3 ship: full-stack CRUD
days.focus: Frontend plus your own API plus a real database, deployed and live.

days.title: Sessions and cookies
days.focus: Understand how a server remembers who you are.

days.title: Email and password auth
days.focus: Hash passwords properly. Never store plaintext.

days.title: OAuth with GitHub
days.focus: Log in with GitHub. The flow recruiters see on every real product.

days.title: Protected routes
days.focus: Server-side route guards, not just hidden buttons.

days.title: File uploads
days.focus: Let users upload an avatar. Validate type and size.

days.title: Roles and permissions
days.focus: Admin sees more than a user. Enforce it on the server.

days.title: Week 4 ship: authed app
days.focus: Your CRUD app, now with real accounts and per-user data.

days.title: WebSockets 101
days.focus: A live counter that updates across two browser tabs.

days.title: Halfway: build a chat room
days.focus: Rooms, messages, presence. You are 30 days in.

days.title: Optimistic updates
days.focus: The UI responds before the server does, and rolls back on failure.

days.title: Animation with intent
days.focus: Motion that explains state changes instead of decorating them.

days.title: Drag and drop
days.focus: A reorderable list that works with touch and keyboard.

days.title: Dark mode done right
days.focus: Token-based theming, respects system preference, no flash on load.

days.title: Week 5 ship: realtime feature
days.focus: Add one genuinely live feature to your product and demo it.

days.title: Measure before you optimise
days.focus: Run Lighthouse. Write down your numbers before touching code.

days.title: Images and fonts
days.focus: The two things that make student projects slow. Fix both.

days.title: Code splitting
days.focus: Ship less JavaScript on first load.

days.title: Your first unit tests
days.focus: Test the logic that would embarrass you if it broke.

days.title: Integration tests
days.focus: Test a whole user flow, not one function.

days.title: CI on every push
days.focus: GitHub Actions runs your tests so you don't have to remember.

days.title: Week 6 ship: green pipeline
days.focus: A repo with a passing CI badge and a Lighthouse score above 90.

days.title: Scope your capstone
days.focus: Write a one-page spec. Cut it in half. Then cut it again.

days.title: Design the data model
days.focus: Tables, relationships, and the queries you'll actually run.

days.title: Build the core flow
days.focus: The one path a user must be able to complete. Nothing else.

days.title: Second flow
days.focus: Now the second most important thing your product does.

days.title: Empty, loading, error
days.focus: Every screen gets all three states. This is what separates students from engineers.

days.title: Mobile pass
days.focus: Open your product at 390px and fix everything that hurts.

days.title: Week 7 ship: usable product
days.focus: Give it to one real person. Watch them use it. Take notes.

days.title: Accessibility audit
days.focus: Keyboard-only navigation and a screen reader pass.

days.title: Handle the edge cases
days.focus: Long names, no data, slow network, double clicks.

days.title: Logging and monitoring
days.focus: Know when your app breaks before your users tell you.

days.title: Deploy properly
days.focus: Custom domain, environment variables, preview deployments.

days.title: Write the README
days.focus: Screenshots, setup steps, architecture, and why you built it.

days.title: Record a 90-second demo
days.focus: Show the product working. No slides.

days.title: Week 8 ship: launch post
days.focus: Post your product publicly and ask for feedback.

days.title: Portfolio rebuild
days.focus: Your 60 days of proof, arranged so a recruiter gets it in 15 seconds.

days.title: Interview-ready stories
days.focus: Three projects, three problems, three decisions you can defend.

days.title: Open-source contribution
days.focus: One real pull request to a project you didn't start.

days.title: The final post
days.focus: 60 days, 60 proofs. Tell the internet what changed.

12.why: Every product you build will eventually need to show data over time. A streak calendar is the smallest honest version of that problem: dense data, tiny screen, must stay readable.
build: Read a JSON array of 60 entries, each with a day number and a status of done, missed or upcoming.
Render one cell per day in a grid, grouped into weeks with a visible week label.
Colour each cell by status and add a tooltip or tap target that reveals the day details.
Make it legible at 390px wide without horizontal scroll.
acceptance: Grid renders from data, not hard-coded markup.
Each cell has an accessible label such as 'Day 12, completed'.
No layout shift when data loads.
12.stretch: Add a hover or long-press card that previews the task title for that day.

1.why: The hardest commit is the first one. Today is about removing every excuse: an account, a repo, one push.
build: Create a public GitHub repository named after your 60-day journey.
Add a README with your name, college, track and what you intend to build.
Make your first commit and push it.
Write a short LinkedIn post announcing that you've started.
acceptance: Repository is public and the README is visible.
At least one commit exists with a meaningful message.
LinkedIn post links to the repository.
1.stretch: Add a profile README to your GitHub account.

11.why: Forms are where most student projects lose users. Validation timing and error copy matter more than the framework you pick.
build: Build a signup form with name, email and password fields.
Validate on blur, not on every keystroke.
Show one clear error message per field, below the field.
Disable submit until the form is valid, and show a pending state on submit.
acceptance: Errors are announced to screen readers.
The form is fully usable with a keyboard.
No error appears before the user has touched a field.
11.stretch: Add a password strength meter that explains what would make it stronger.

13.why: Two components that need the same data is the most common React confusion. Solving it once fixes a hundred future bugs.
build: Render a searchable list where the search input and the list are separate components.
Hold the query in the closest common parent.
Show a result count and an empty state when nothing matches.
acceptance: No duplicated state between the two children.
Empty state is designed, not blank.
13.stretch: Persist the last query in the URL so results are shareable.
